newsitem.title: USA: Ex-CIA employee pleads guilty in pornography case.
newsitem.headline: Ex-CIA employee pleads guilty in pornography case.

text.p: A former CIA employee pleaded guilty on Thursday to possessing child pornography on a computer in his home and to a financial conflict-of-interest charge, the Justice Department said.
It said David Miller, 54, who resigned from the CIA last month instead of being fired immediately, admitted his guilt during a hearing at a federal court in Alexandria, Virginia.

Miller acknowledged that while employed by the CIA and on detail to the government's National Reconnaissance Organisation, he made unauthorised personal use of a government computer he had taken home.
The Justice Department said he used the computer to obtain through America Online 10 pornographic files, some of which showed minors engaged in sexually explicit conduct.

Miller also admitted he arranged for a friend to be hired by a government contractor involving contracts he supervised when the friend owed Miller and his wife $18,500, but was unable to repay the money.
Miller faces a maximum 10-year prison term at his sentencing, scheduled in January.
